analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject, and אֹתָם (“them”) identifies the people he caused to disperse. מִשָּׁם marks their point of departure, and עַל־פְּנֵי כָל־הָאָרֶץ describes the extent of their dispersal. As a result, they stopped building the city.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject יַהְוֶה.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ means “over the face of the whole earth.” The phrase describes where Yahweh scattered them.
analysis.morphology: Independent Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
Common noun, common gender, plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, הָאָרֶץ denotes the earth as a single whole. כָל marks the full extent of the scattering, “over the face of the whole earth.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ means “over the face of the whole earth.” The phrase gives the extent of the people’s dispersal from the city.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes אָרֶץ, the definite-context form of אֶרֶץ. The noun is common gender, singular, and absolute.
